name: Captured Surface Control (scroll and zoom the shared tab)
plain: Lets an app scroll and zoom the tab it is capturing.
meaning: Gives a meeting app remote scroll and zoom of the person's own shared tab. Needs a separate prompt because it is a control action on top of a view.

web.api: CaptureController.sendWheel(), setZoomLevel(), getZoomLevel(), oncapturedzoomchange; permission captured-surface-control

access.prompt_ui: A permission prompt appears when the controller is first used, only if the captured surface is a same-site tab.
access.revocation: Stops with the capture or by revoking in Site settings

data.metric: Wheel and zoom control of the captured tab

limits.headline: Can scroll and zoom the browser tab it is sharing, if from the same site
limits.user_action: You share a tab in a presentation or recording tool, then use its scroll or zoom buttons
can: Scroll the shared tab up and down from the controlling app
Zoom the shared tab in or out
Check the current zoom level so the controls stay in sync
cannot: Control a tab from a different site or a window or screen share
Do anything before you pick the tab to share
Click, type or fill forms in the shared tab
Work in Firefox, Safari, Chrome on Android or iPhone browsers
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome and Edge support it.

story.what_it_is: Lets a meeting app scroll and zoom the tab you are sharing, from inside the call.

marketing.name: Captured Surface Control
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes it as letting a meeting app scroll and zoom the shared tab, so presenters do not switch windows.

story.for_you: After you share a tab in a call, a second prompt asks if the call site may scroll and zoom that tab. If you allow it, a slide may advance when someone presses a button in the call window, with no tab switch.
story.for_makers: Call sites want presenters and remote helpers to flip slides or zoom a doc from inside the meeting view. It makes a web meeting feel closer to a real room. It is a feature meeting makers can brag about over rivals.

use_cases.example: In a Google Meet call, you share a slides tab and move to the next slide from the Meet window without clicking back and forth.
A teacher shares a worksheet tab and a helper student scrolls to the next question in the call view during a remote lesson.
A sales rep shares a product demo tab, and a colleague on the call zooms in on a chart when asked, with the rep's approval.
A designer shares a Figma tab in a review, and the client zooms in on a corner of the design to point out an issue.
An engineer shares a dashboard tab, and a teammate scrolls the log view during a live bug hunt.
A low vision participant zooms in on the shared tab to read small text without asking the presenter to change anything.

risks: Remote control of what is on your screen

technical_bounds: Only for tab capture of a same-origin or permitted document
No pointer clicks or keyboard injection

legit_uses: Presenting slides from a separate control window
abuse: Scroll-jacking a shared tab if over-trusted
